chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man who ate an egg of a dove of the Haram, while he was in Ihram. He said: Upon him, for each egg, is blood (of a sacrificial animal), and upon him is its price, a sixth or a quarter of a Dirham. (The word 'al-wahm' is from Salih).

Then he said: The blood (of a sacrificial animal) is necessitated upon him for eating it while he was in Ihram; and the penalty (of its price) is necessitated upon him for taking an egg of a dove of the Haram.

key_terms.حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ: Doves of the Haram (specifically those in Mecca)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood (a type of sacrificial animal penalty)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for eating a dove's egg while in Ihram inside the Haram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that a person in Ihram who eats an egg of a dove from the Haram must provide both the blood of a sacrificial animal (dam) and pay the monetary value (kaffarah) of the egg. The ruling distinguishes between the penalty for the act of eating while in the state of consecration and the penalty for taking the specific prey. This hadith highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'ta'addud al-dam' (multiplicity of penalties), where distinct violations—such as consuming prohibited food versus capturing specific game—incurred separate compensations, reflecting the nuanced application of Quranic hunting laws in the sacred precincts. Additionally, the specific valuation of the egg (one-sixth or one-fourth of a dirham) provides insight into the economic context of Mecca during the early Islamic period.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘Heasws was asked about a man who ate an egg of a dove of the Harram, and he was in Ihraam’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him, for each egg, is blood (of a sacrificial animal), and upon him is its price, being a sixth or a quarter Dirham for being deluded from correctness’.

Then heasws said: ‘The blood (of a sacrificial animal) is necessitated upon him for eating it, and he was in Ihraam; and the penalty (of its price) is necessitated on him for taking an egg of a dove of the Harram’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-ffusayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il from Salih ibn ’Uqbah from al- Harith ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who while in the state of Ihram eats the egg of pigeons of al-Haram (the sacred area). He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes one animal offering for each egg as well as the cost of each egg which is about one-sixth or one-fourth of one dirham in a settlement.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘The animal offering is obligatory because of his eating them in the state of Ihram and the penalty of payment of the cost of eggs is because of his taking them in al- Haram (the sacred area).”’
